paper_title: An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment   of COVID-19 vaccines
caption: : Polarity scores for Indonesia
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the distribution of polarity scores for vaccine-related sentiments in Indonesia, as analyzed in the paper “An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment of COVID-19 vaccines.” The x-axis, labeled “Polarity scores,” spans from -1.0 to 0.6, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2, representing a linear scale of sentiment ranging from strongly negative to moderately positive. The y-axis, labeled “Counts,” ranges from 0 to 35,000 in increments of 5,000, indicating the frequency of occurrences for each polarity score bin. A single blue line with circular markers connects the data points, showing a general trend: counts remain near zero for polarity scores from -1.0 to -0.7, then gradually increase, peaking sharply at a polarity score of 0.0 with approximately 35,000 counts. Following this peak, the counts decline steeply to around 12,000 at 0.1, rise again to about 17,500 at 0.2, then drop to roughly 6,000 at 0.3, fall to near 0 at 0.4, rise slightly to about 6,000 at 0.5, and end at approximately 0 at 0.6. The plot reveals a strong concentration of sentiment around neutral (0.0) with a long tail toward negative scores and a more erratic, lower-frequency distribution on the positive side.
